scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) and not the author's working copy. MapSplat is a QGIS plugin (Python, runs inside QGIS) that exports a static web map bundle. It has no web framework; the only listening HTTP server is the serve.py helper that exporter.py writes into the export output (string template in exporter.py around lines 3040-3300). Shell (scripts/*.sh, Makefile), PowerShell (deploy.ps1) and one Node script (scripts/gen_basemap_styles.mjs) are present; full interface/data-access detection for those languages is out of scope for skill version 1.0 and they were only read for deps/hosts/secrets. Excluded: test fixtures (test/*.py sample paths such as C:/Users/me/...), the embedded PDF-writer JavaScript in exporter.py (false positive for Windows-path grep), generated/binary docs, and basemap_styles/*.json vendored Protomaps styles. Authenticated routes: none exist; the single route entry is the generated static file handler.

python.package_manager: none (plugin runs inside QGIS; dev tools run via 'uv run --no-project --with ...')
findings: No requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or lockfile: runtime dependencies (QGIS/PyQt, GDAL/ogr2ogr, pmtiles CLI) are provided by the host environment and are not declared in a manifest.
Dev tools (ruff, flake8, bandit, detect-secrets, pytest) are fetched unpinned by 'uv run --with' in Makefile and .github/workflows/ci.yml.
scripts/gen_basemap_styles.mjs requires @protomaps/basemaps but there is no package.json or lockfile (dev-time script only).

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: detect-secrets baseline enforced in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and pre-commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml)
states the plugin does not handle authentication or store credentials

routes.path: /* (static files of the exported map directory; also OPTIONS and HTTP Range requests)
routes.note: Template for serve.py written next to exported maps: SimpleHTTPRequestHandler subclass with Range support and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'. Binds 127.0.0.1 by default (--host default at exporter.py:3064); user may pass --host 0.0.0.0. Serves only the exported static map files; no application data or auth by design.

interfaces.network_binding: 127.0.0.1 by default for generated serve.py (0.0.0.0 only via --host)

sql_injection_risk.reason: sqlite3 used only to read metadata from a user-chosen MBTiles file; no string-built SQL found.

external_apis.host: unpkg.com (MapLibre GL JS and PMTiles JS bundles, downloaded for offline mode and referenced by exported viewer)
build.protomaps.com / maps.protomaps.com / protomaps.github.io (basemap PMTiles and styles)
tile.openstreetmap.org, basemaps.cartocdn.com, server.arcgisonline.com, a.tile.opentopomap.org (XYZ basemap tiles)
user-supplied basemap/style URLs (HEAD/ranged GET probe, https/http only)

file_system_access.detail: writes export bundle (index.html, style.json, PMTiles, lib/, serve.py, README.txt) to a user-chosen output folder; removes temporary GPKG files and temp dirs
appends to a plugin log file
runs ogr2ogr / ogrinfo / pmtiles CLIs through subprocess.run with list arguments (no shell=True) on exported layer data

what_this_app_can_do: Exports the layers, styling, labels and layer order of the open QGIS project into a self-contained static web map (PMTiles plus MapLibre GL JS).
Runs ogr2ogr/GDAL and the pmtiles command line tool on the user's own layer data to build tiles.
Optionally downloads MapLibre/PMTiles scripts and probes basemap URLs on the internet.
Writes a serve.py helper that starts a local static web server (127.0.0.1 by default) with CORS open to all origins to preview the exported map.

data_sources_touched.source: QGIS project layers chosen by the user (files/databases already loaded in QGIS)
Output folder bundle on local disk or a static host the user copies it to
Public basemap/tile hosts (Protomaps, OpenStreetMap, Carto, Esri, OpenTopoMap) and unpkg.com

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: A desktop QGIS plugin used by whoever runs QGIS. The optional generated serve.py binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and has no authentication; it is reachable from the network only if started with --host 0.0.0.0. Exported maps are static and intended to be published publicly if hosted.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Generated serve.py sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and has no authentication (reachable beyond localhost if --host 0.0.0.0).
Exported viewer loads MapLibre and PMTiles from unpkg.com unless offline bundling is chosen.
Exported map bundles contain the user's layer data, which becomes public if the folder is hosted publicly.

top_findings: No secrets or committed secret files; detect-secrets and bandit run in CI
Generated serve.py has open CORS and no auth (binds 127.0.0.1 by default)
No dependency manifest or lockfile; dev tools fetched unpinned
